director.chapterArc: Methodical experimentation turns an accidental mechanical insight into a workable system; tactical planning then forces Callie to defend the limits of her power and her right to choose the risk. Her mother’s claim to one borrowed good day shifts the chapter from logistics into restrained anticipatory grief. Dawn converts that choice into action: the family separates into assigned positions, the tackle is set, and the chapter closes in taut stillness as the first pull begins.
director.restraintNote: Keep Original Calder grounded, observant, and mechanically precise. Discoveries are data before wonder; fear appears as counting, narrowed attention, and physical preparation. Let the mother’s mortality register without vocal fracture, and treat the ash as borrowed function rather than a miracle. Do not accelerate the technical passages: the hook, blocks, line, horse, road, and human positions must remain spatially clear. Every colored passage returns fully to Calder’s base identity.

cues.delivery: Catch Otto’s unpolished correction with dry gentleness; he is embarrassed by his own useful observation, not playing for a laugh.
cues.from: "The pipe's not yours," said Otto. He went red. "I mean — it's not hers. Your grandfather's. The hook was his for sixty years. The pipe came out of a wall."
cues.through: "The pipe's not yours," said Otto. He went red. "I mean — it's not hers. Your grandfather's. The hook was his for sixty years. The pipe came out of a wall."
cues.reason: Otto’s self-correction provides the first small human release inside the experiment.

cues.delivery: Let Callie’s formal thanks wrong-foot Otto; keep the exchange spare, with the blush supplying the comedy rather than a comic voice.
cues.through: "Oh," said Otto, and went a different shade of red, and looked at his boots.
cues.reason: The awkward gratitude briefly releases the pressure of the breakthrough.

cues.delivery: Use controlled scientific astonishment: the impossible persistence of the pale is observed as a physical fact, then endangered by Callie’s attention. Keep the mechanics foremost.
cues.from: She said, "Ask Pell, I don't know horses," and turned back, and the pale was still in the steel.
cues.through: She looked at it. She looked at it hard, the way you look at a thing you're afraid is going to fall. And as she looked at it, the pale began to go thin at the point. She stepped forward and got her hand back on it, fast, and it held for another four or five seconds, and went out.
cues.reason: The pale remaining in the untouched hook materially changes Callie’s understanding of her power.

cues.delivery: Give Katori’s comparison a dry, exact edge; the joke is a practical description, not an invitation to linger.
cues.from: "It did. I watched it. You turned round and talked to Otto about a strap, and it stood there. Then you turned back and looked at it like it owed you money, and it started to go."
cues.through: "It did. I watched it. You turned round and talked to Otto about a strap, and it stood there. Then you turned back and looked at it like it owed you money, and it started to go."
cues.reason: Katori uses understated humor to state the otherwise inexplicable result.

cues.delivery: Narrow inward as Callie connects gripping the hook to watching her mother breathe; reveal the survival compulsion without sentimentality or rising melodrama.
cues.from: Callie did not know what to do with that. She had spent the whole of her life learning that the way to keep hold of a thing was to hold it harder. The way to keep hold of a hook was to grip it. The way to keep hold of a sack was to watch it all the way down. The way to keep your mother alive was never to stop watching her breathe.
cues.through: Callie did not know what to do with that. She had spent the whole of her life learning that the way to keep hold of a thing was to hold it harder. The way to keep hold of a hook was to grip it. The way to keep hold of a sack was to watch it all the way down. The way to keep your mother alive was never to stop watching her breathe.
cues.reason: The mechanical discovery exposes the private fear governing Callie’s vigilance.

cues.delivery: Land Pell’s request with bleak logistical deadpan. He is naming the failure condition honestly, not making light of it.
cues.from: "Then it's longer than forty seconds," said Pell, "and I'll be sitting on the brake of a wagon hanging off a hook in a crack, and I'd be grateful if you'd think of something."
cues.through: "Then it's longer than forty seconds," said Pell, "and I'll be sitting on the brake of a wagon hanging off a hook in a crack, and I'd be grateful if you'd think of something."
cues.reason: The line’s grim humor sharpens rather than softens the danger.

cues.delivery: Keep Katori authoritative and factual, with protective intent held underneath the insistence that her safer proposal be formally heard.
cues.from: "It's a good plan," said Katori. "It's the one I'd make with anybody else. I want it said."
cues.through: "It's a good plan," said Katori. "It's the one I'd make with anybody else. I want it said."
cues.reason: Her advocacy is driven by protection, though she presents it as procedure.

cues.delivery: Name Callie’s unspoken wish quietly and without exposing her; Katori grants permission while preserving Callie’s dignity.
cues.from: "And there's a thing you didn't say," said Katori, not looking up, "which is that you'd rather your mother wasn't on this hill for three days. I'm saying it for you. You're allowed that too."
cues.through: "And there's a thing you didn't say," said Katori, not looking up, "which is that you'd rather your mother wasn't on this hill for three days. I'm saying it for you. You're allowed that too."
cues.reason: Katori recognizes that Callie’s tactical refusal also protects her mother.

cues.delivery: Give the mother even, self-possessed warmth. This is a claim to spend her own remaining strength while being present for Callie, never a plea.
cues.from: "There's a jar in the bottom of the barrow," she said. "Five handfuls. You lifted all of them. I know exactly where every one of them came from, because I was lying on a plank in the road waiting for you to come back from each one." Her voice was very even. "You were going to put that on the table at the gate, so they'd see we could pay. And Katori's standing for us at the gate now, and your tenth is in Pell's book. So I want one of them. For the hill. I want one good day, and I want to spend it on walking up that hill on my own two feet, and seeing you at the top of it."
cues.through: "There's a jar in the bottom of the barrow," she said. "Five handfuls. You lifted all of them. I know exactly where every one of them came from, because I was lying on a plank in the road waiting for you to come back from each one." Her voice was very even. "You were going to put that on the table at the gate, so they'd see we could pay. And Katori's standing for us at the gate now, and your tenth is in Pell's book. So I want one of them. For the hill. I want one good day, and I want to spend it on walking up that hill on my own two feet, and seeing you at the top of it."
cues.reason: Her request for one good day is both an assertion of autonomy and an act of maternal devotion.

cues.delivery: Let the finality settle under her steady boundary, then leave Callie’s inability to answer unadorned. No break, sob, or consoling cadence.
cues.from: "It's mine to spend," said her mother. "You said it yourself, today, to Pell, about your tenth. It's mine. I'm saying it now." She held Callie's eyes. "You don't get to spend me, love. Not even on keeping me."
cues.through: Callie could not say anything at all.
cues.reason: The mother states that Callie cannot preserve her by taking away her agency.

cues.delivery: Move into close, wakeful alarm through changed breathing and the repetitive hand motion. Keep observation exact; terror is contained by recognition and readiness.
cues.from: Her mother went off in the night, a little after two.
cues.through: Her mother's eyes were half open. Her right hand was moving on the blanket, the same small plucking motion as on the morning before the causeway. She was picking at a thread that was not there, over and over.
cues.reason: The mother’s nighttime episode turns anticipated loss into an immediate physical threat.

cues.delivery: Make each reassurance soft, immediate, and functional—Callie is trying to anchor her mother without waking or frightening the camp.
cues.from: "I'm here," said Callie. "I'm here. I'm here."
cues.through: "I'm here," said Callie. "I'm here. I'm here."
cues.reason: The repeated intimate reassurance is genuinely hushed and urgent.

cues.delivery: Let the unimpeded touch carry more than the words. The command to sleep is practical maternal care, with no farewell coloring.
cues.from: "Good." Her mother's left hand came out from under the blanket and found Callie's wrist, and held it. It did not stop a finger's width short of anything. "Go to sleep. You've got a hill."
cues.through: "Good." Her mother's left hand came out from under the blanket and found Callie's wrist, and held it. It did not stop a finger's width short of anything. "Go to sleep. You've got a hill."
cues.reason: Physical contact briefly restores their ordinary mother-daughter bond.

cues.delivery: Keep the mother’s line lightly factual, almost weather-report plain; allow the first spoken naming of death to register beneath it without a vocal catch.
cues.from: "Give it a minute, love. I've been dying for three months, I can wait a minute to feel better." She said it lightly. It was the first time she had ever said the word, and she said it the way you'd say it was going to rain, and she went straight on. "Where's my hat?"
cues.through: "Give it a minute, love. I've been dying for three months, I can wait a minute to feel better." She said it lightly. It was the first time she had ever said the word, and she said it the way you'd say it was going to rain, and she went straight on. "Where's my hat?"
cues.reason: She says aloud what both have avoided, then immediately continues with ordinary business.

cues.delivery: Register the unfamiliar borrowed capacity with quiet recognition, not miraculous uplift. Her lighter voice remains fragile and finite.
cues.from: "Oh," she said, in a slightly different voice. "Oh, yes. I see."
cues.through: "It's a good day," said her mother. "Somebody's lent me a good day. I don't know who, and I'm not going to ask." She looked up the long pale cut to the sky. "Ines. You said there was a way up the red earth. Take me up it. I'd like to be at the top before anybody needs me to be anywhere."
cues.reason: The ash grants a tangible but temporary good day.

cues.delivery: Widen gently to the two figures on the rim, then make the held-arm answer private and exact. Do not turn the gesture into a farewell.
cues.from: They went up the road together, the woman who shot and the woman who could not braid her own hair, arm in arm, slowly. At the bottom of the steep part they turned off onto a cattle track up the red earth at the side of the cut. Callie watched them all the way, until they were two small figures on the rim of the cut against the sky, a long way up. One of them lifted an arm. Not a wave. It was held up, flat, the way you hold something up to be seen.
cues.through: Callie held her arm up back.
cues.reason: The distant reciprocal gesture carries restrained connection before Callie returns to work.

cues.delivery: Hold quiet threat in Katori’s exposed sentinel position; describe her stillness and the unopened Ember as deliberate readiness, not foreboding spectacle.
cues.from: Katori looked at her for a moment. Then she nodded once and went up the road to the lip, and stood on the top of the scarp with her back to Callie and her face to the high plain. She did not take her Ember out.
cues.through: Katori looked at her for a moment. Then she nodded once and went up the road to the lip, and stood on the top of the scarp with her back to Callie and her face to the high plain. She did not take her Ember out.
cues.reason: Katori faces the unseen high plain alone as the operation becomes irreversible.

cues.delivery: Tighten into high-tension stillness while preserving every mechanical step. The final command is low because distance and still air carry it; urgency must not become speed or volume.
cues.from: The pale went into the hook.
cues.through: "Pull," Callie said. She said it not very loud, because the air was still, and on the top of the scarp Otto heard her and said it again to the horse. "Pull."
cues.reason: The pale engages, the brake releases, and the first pull commits everyone to the plan.
